summary: David Kopf (1930–2023) was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Chicago from circa 1955 to 1964. He held a post at the University of Minnesota from circa 1967 to 1999.
David L. Gosling is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, Cambridge in 1992 and held an attested post at the University of Cambridge in 2001.

David L. Haberman is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Colorado Boulder (~1971–1976). He held posts at the University of Arizona (~1989–1993) and Indiana University (~1993).

David L. McMahan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He taught at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and the University of Vermont, and served as Assistant Professor (attested 2002) and Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2013) at Franklin & Marshall College.

David L. Snellgrove (1920–2016) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge under D. R. Shackleton Bailey, H. W. Bailey, and Walter Simon, as well as Giuseppe Tucci. He held posts at SOAS and the University of London (~1950–1982).
David Ludden is a historian and Indologist. He held academic posts at the University of Virginia (~1978–1979), the University of Pennsylvania (~1979–2007), and New York University (~2007).

David M. DiValerio works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the School for International Training and the University of Virginia (PhD under Kurtis R. Schaeffer). In 2015, he held an attested post at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee.

David M. Knipe is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as Professor (attested 1975, 1998–2001) and Professor of South Asian Studies and Chair of Religious Studies (attested 1989).
David Matsumoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as Director (attested 2004) and held an attested post in 2013 at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.
David N. Keightley (1932–2017) was a sinologist and historian. He held posts at the University of California, Berkeley, where he was attested as a professor in 1985 and was attested in 1999.

David N. Lorenzen is an Indologist and historian. He studied at SOAS and the Australian National University under A. L. Basham. From circa 1972 to 2015, he was a professor and researcher at El Colegio de México's Center of Asian and African Studies.

David Ownby is a sinologist and historian of religion. He completed his PhD at Harvard University (~1980–1989) and worked there in 1991. He taught at Southern Methodist University (attested 1994) and served as Professor of History at Université de Montréal (~1993–2023).

David P. Jackson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA, MA, and PhD at the University of Washington, studying under David Seyfort Ruegg, and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).

David Patt is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1993) under the supervision of Geshe Lhundub Sopa, also studying under Geshe Lobsang Tenzin and Geshe Thubten Tandhar.

David Phillip Stanley specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He has served as associate professor at Naropa University and Co-Director of the Nitartha Institute (attested 2019).

David Pingree (1933–2005) worked in Indology and history. He studied at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Otto Neugebauer. He held posts at Harvard, Chicago, the American University of Beirut, the Institute for Advanced Study, and Brown University.

David R. Loy works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Carleton College, the University of Hawaii, and the National University of Singapore (PhD, 1984), where he taught. He later served as Besl Family Professor at Xavier University (~2007–2009).

David Ralph Quinter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned an MA at the University of Colorado Boulder and a PhD at Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, later joining the University of Alberta (attested 2019).

David Roy Shackleton Bailey (1917–2005) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. After studying at Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge, he held posts there, at Jesus College, at the University of Michigan (1968–1975), and at Harvard University (1975–1982).
David Ruddell (1943–2015) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Laval University and served as Secretary at Fort William College.
